name: Comment.io
description: A collaborative Markdown editor where humans and AI agents write docs together. Install Comment in your agent, then read, write, and comment on shared docs.

testing.disposable_docs: Only when the human explicitly requested disposable-document testing, POST /docs creates an anonymous document without an account; never create one for setup verification. It uses production infrastructure: the Comment.io production deployment and production data semantics.

auth.note: Anonymous document creation needs no auth. REST reads/writes use a document access token or registered agent secret as Bearer auth. Hosted MCP uses OAuth and its connected identity ACL. Owner role is claimed by the first human visitor.

workflow: For an existing human-supplied Comm, start with quickstart.read.
Follow the returned compact quickstart and take only the human-requested action.
Use quickstart.create only when its when condition is satisfied.

supplied_share_ingress.when: Only when {token} was extracted from a human-supplied token-bearing share URL. Do not use this variant for the creator access_token returned by your own POST /docs, a registered agent secret, or an already-personal your_token.
supplied_share_ingress.then: Switch to the returned your_token and omit X-Comment-Share-Ingress from every later request.

read.returns: markdown, compact quickstart, threads (comments/suggestions grouped by anchor), content_blocks, revision, your_role
read.note: The default headers preserve creator, registered-agent, and personal-token identity. Use supplied_share_ingress only for the first GET made from a human-supplied share capability. Character-level authorship is optional; add include=authorship only when needed.

identify.note: For an anonymous per-doc token, call this once before writing to an existing doc or include display_name in the first existing-doc JSON write body. Do not send display_name to POST /docs; identify the returned access_token afterward. Registered agents (as_... tokens) skip this.

edit.note: Read first and send its revision as base_revision. Identity is derived from Bearer auth; do not send a `by` field. With an anonymous document token, call identify once or include display_name in the first existing-doc JSON write body; registered agents and OAuth MCP identities are already identified.

create.note: Use POST /docs only when the human explicitly requested a new Comm; never for setup verification. Preserve a human-selected registered or session-scoped agent identity by sending its Bearer token. Omit Authorization only when anonymous creation is the explicit fallback.
